ai.literal: assembly having-known having-examined let-speak of-words collection who-knew purity they
ai.translation: Let the pure who know the rich multitude of words examine their speech and deliver it with a clear understanding of the assembly.
ai.modern: சொற்களின் வகைகளை அறிந்த தூய்மையானவர்கள், அவையின் தன்மையை அறிந்து ஆராய்ந்து பேச வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of understanding one's audience before speaking. The phrase 'சொல்லின் தொகை' refers to a rich vocabulary or the full range of words available to a speaker. The poet states that even those who possess this pure and vast knowledge of words must carefully examine what they are going to say. They must tailor their speech to suit the nature and capacity of the assembly they are addressing.

ai.literal: Context having known, well having perceived, let speak; of words the course who knew, goodness they.
ai.translation: Let the good people who know the proper usage of words speak only after understanding the context and perceiving the audience well.
ai.modern: சொற்களின் நடையை அறிந்த நல்லவர்கள், அவையின் தன்மையை அறிந்து நன்கு உணர்ந்த பின்பே பேச வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of understanding one's audience before speaking. The phrase 'சொல்லின் நடை' refers to the proper course or usage of words, highlighting the skill of effective communication. The word 'இடை' denotes the context or the assembly. The poet stresses that even good people who master vocabulary must carefully perceive the situation to ensure their words are appropriate and well-received.

ai.literal: Assembly they-know-not speaking upon those-who-take of-words nature they-know-not capable-thing-even is-not.
ai.translation: Those who undertake to speak without understanding their audience do not know the nature of words, and they possess no real ability.
ai.modern: அவையின் தன்மையை அறியாமல் பேசத் தொடங்குபவர்கள், சொற்களின் தன்மையையும் அறியாதவர்கள்; அவர்களுக்கு என்று எந்தத் திறமையும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of understanding one's audience before speaking. If a person begins to speak without assessing the assembly, it shows they do not truly understand how to use words effectively. Consequently, whatever other skills they might claim to have are rendered useless and non-existent.

ai.literal: Brilliant ones before, bright ones becoming; blank ones before, pure chalk color taking.
ai.translation: Be brilliant before those who are brilliant. Before those who are unlearned, take on the plain color of pure white chalk.
ai.modern: அறிவுடையோர் முன்னே தாமும் அறிவுடையவராகப் பேசவேண்டும். அறிவில்லாதவர் முன்னே தாமும் வெண்சுதை போல ஒன்றும் அறியாதவராக எளிமையாக இருக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises adapting one's discourse to the audience. Before an assembly of brilliant and learned people, a speaker should display their own brilliance. However, before an unlearned or blank audience, the speaker should assume the plainness of pure white chalk, keeping their words simple and unadorned. The contrast between light and blankness emphasizes the need to match the intellectual level of the listeners.

ai.literal: good said those among even good indeed elders among advancing not speaking restraint
ai.translation: Even among all things considered good, the restraint of not rushing to speak before elders is truly excellent.
ai.modern: நல்லவை என்று சொல்லப்பட்ட எல்லாவற்றுள்ளும், அறிவில் முதிர்ந்தவர் அவையில் முந்திக்கொண்டு பேசாத அடக்கமே மிகவும் நல்லதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the virtue of humility and restraint in an assembly. The phrase 'முந்து கிளவாச் செறிவு' refers to the composure of holding back and not speaking out of turn before those who are older and wiser. The poet declares that among all recognized virtues, this specific restraint is exceptionally good.

ai.literal: From the path / position / having faltered / like that indeed / vast / knowledge / having accepted / those who understand / in front of / slip.
ai.translation: Making a slip before an audience that grasps vast knowledge is exactly like losing one's footing and falling from the path.
ai.modern: பரந்த அறிவினை ஏற்று உணரும் அறிஞர்கள் முன்னே பேசும்போது பிழை செய்வது, நடக்கும் வழியில் நிலைதடுமாறி விழுவதற்குச் சமமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares making a mistake while speaking to a learned audience to physically slipping and falling on a path. The word 'ஆறு' means a path or way, and 'நிலை தளர்ந்து' means losing one's balance or footing. The phrase 'வியன் புலம் ஏற்று உணர்வார்' refers to scholars who possess vast knowledge and can readily grasp what is being said. A slip of the tongue or an error in logic in front of such an audience is as dangerous and irreversible as losing one's footing on a journey.

ai.literal: Having learned, those who have understood - [their] learning - will shine - fault - to be removed - word - examining - those who are capable - in [their] presence.
ai.translation: The education of those who have learned and understood will shine in the presence of those capable of flawlessly examining words.
ai.modern: குற்றமில்லாமல் சொற்களை ஆராய்ந்து அறியும் வல்லமை பெற்றவர்களின் அவையில்தான், கற்று அறிந்தவர்களின் கல்வி பெருமையுடன் விளங்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the ideal environment for true knowledge to be recognized. The phrase 'கசடறச் சொல் தெரிதல் வல்லார்' refers to experts who can flawlessly analyze and evaluate words and their profound meanings. The word 'அகத்து' means 'in the presence of' or 'in the assembly'. The poet asserts that the education of a learned person will truly shine ('விளங்கும்') and be fully appreciated only when presented before such a discerning audience.

ai.literal: Understanding those who possess in front of speaking, of that which grows in the bed water having poured it is like.
ai.translation: Speaking before an audience that possesses deep understanding is like pouring water into the bed of a growing plant.
ai.modern: உணர்வாற்றல் உடையவர்களுக்கு முன்னால் ஒரு கருத்தைப் பேசுவது, வளரும் பயிரின் பாத்தியில் நீரை ஊற்றுவதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates the value of addressing a receptive and intelligent audience. The phrase 'உணர்வது உடையார்' denotes those who possess the sensibility to truly grasp what is spoken. When ideas are shared with such an assembly, they are nurtured and allowed to flourish. The poet compares this to pouring water directly into the prepared bed of a growing plant, where the nourishment is fully absorbed and leads to fruitful growth.

ai.literal: In a mean assembly, even forgetfully, let them not speak, in a good assembly well to reach those who speak.
ai.translation: Those who can speak well and convincingly in an assembly of the good should never, even forgetfully, speak in an assembly of the ignorant.
ai.modern: நல்லோர் அவையில் கருத்துக்கள் நன்றாகப் பதியும்படி பேசும் திறமையுடையவர்கள், அறிவில்லாதவர்களின் அவையில் மறந்தும் பேசக்கூடாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises wise speakers to avoid sharing their knowledge with an unworthy audience. The phrase 'நல்லவையுள் நன்கு சலச் சொல்லுவார்' refers to those who have the skill to speak effectively and be well-received among the learned (note: 'சல' here functions as a variant of 'செல', meaning to go, reach, or be accepted). Such capable people are warned not to speak 'புல்லவையுள்' (in a mean or ignorant assembly) even by mistake ('பொச்சாந்தும்'). Speaking to those who cannot appreciate the message is a waste of wisdom and diminishes the speaker's dignity.

ai.literal: Inside the drain spilled ambrosia it is like, one's own group-members those who are not in front of discourse holding.
ai.translation: Holding a discourse before those who are not of one's own kind is like spilling ambrosia into a dirty drain.
ai.modern: தமது தகுதியைப் போன்ற தகுதி இல்லாதவர்கள் முன்னே ஒரு பொருளைப் பற்றிப் பேசுவது, சாக்கடையில் சிந்திய அமிழ்தத்தைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: The couplet warns against sharing valuable knowledge with an unreceptive or unsuited audience. 'கோட்டி கொளல்' means holding a discourse or sharing profound words. Doing this before people who are not of one's own kind ('தம் கணத்தார் அல்லார் முன்')—meaning those who lack the refinement or understanding to appreciate it—is a waste. The poet compares this to 'அமிழ்து' (ambrosia), the most precious and life-giving substance, being spilled into an 'அங்கணம்' (a dirty drain), where it is completely ruined and useless.
